title: Crime or kangaroo court? Rock River debates 'charges' against planning commissioners - NewsBreak
text:
By Schyler Perkins ,
1 days ago
There is a better way to read this story. Download the My UP Now app for your apple or android device.
ROCK RIVER TOWNSHIP, Mich. (WJMN/WBUP) — Two civil servants in Rock River Township could be removed from the planning commission amid allegations they committed malfeasance in office.
Meanwhile, critics wonder if the claims are driven by an ulterior motive.
Rock River contains several small communities along M-94 between Marquette and Munising, with populations adding up to about 1,200. Our previous report about the community details a recent effort to repeal local zoning laws as one trustee sues the township — over what he argues is an improper denial from the zoning board.
While that trustee, Jim Rondeau, denies any involvement in the effort to repeal zoning, some members of the community are unconvinced.
BACKGROUND | 'It angers me': Twp. leader denies Eben Ice Caves lawsuit linked to zoning repeal effort
On Friday, a last-minute special meeting was called at the Rock River Township Hall to “discuss written charges on two planning commission members and consider scheduling public removal hearings.”
While a number of residents told My UP News they were caught off-guard and were confused by the announcement, word had begun to circulate that planners Olivia Kingery and Tammy Shega were the subjects of scrutiny by Township Trustee Victor Aho.
During the initial period of public comment, several frustrated community members said their piece.
“As a taxpayer and resident, I am fed up with the clown show that you people are leading here,” said one resident. “This is a kangaroo court.”
“This is such a sham,” said another. “ This seems like incredibly convenient timing to have these grievances brought up. These alleged charges against Tammy and Olivia seem incredibly convenient when we're in the middle of a very contentious zoning vote.”
Deputy Township Supervisor Trevor Case also criticized the meeting, saying, “I don't have a better word besides corruption that's happening in this community right now. And yes, you're not their pawn. You are not their pawn. You’re their absolute b****.”
Later, Case specified the statement was aimed at Aho, referencing a previous comment where Case accused Aho of being at Rondeau's beck and call.
Aho presents the charges
Trustee Victor Aho said the accusations he had collected against Kingery and Shega were the product of six months of investigating the issues, including a concerted effort leading up to the meeting.
“I've been up for two weeks straight, all night long. Why? So we can start following the rules around here,” said Aho. “It's got everything required right down to them owing us money for unlawful charges to this township, that our taxpayers paid for.”
At different times, Aho also described the alleged crimes as “malfeasance” and “pure negligence.”
Aho also described the process for removal, saying the special meeting was called for the purpose of presenting the charges and considering whether the board should call a removal hearing.
“If there is a public hearing, [evidence] will be presented and everybody will get their chance to rebut and prove [their] innocence or prove guilt at that time,” said Aho.
Aho then read his statement of charges against Kingery.
A copy of the written charges provided to My UP News by Kingery lists the charges as follows:
Unauthorized legal contact and expenditure; related to Kingery engaging in “unauthorized contact with legal counsel regarding township business” on three occasionsUltra Vires Acts/Operating outside of scope; related to initiating legal consultations without formal authorizationCreation of public financial liability; related to incurring a cost to the township by speaking with the attorneyViolation of public trust; related to a “willful circumvention” of township bylaws
During the meeting, commissioners also discussed claims that Kingery withheld or failed to deliver planning commission documents to Clerk Heather Marsh, though those accusations do not appear to be reflected in the document delivered to Kingery.
The charges against Shega include:
unauthorized legal contact and expenditure; related to Shega engaging in “unauthorized contact with legal counsel regarding township business” on three occasionsUltra Vires Acts/Operating outside of scope; related to initiating legal consultations without formal authorizationCreation of public financial liability; related to incurring a cost to the township by speaking with the attorneyViolation of public trust; related to a “willful circumvention” of township bylawsViolation of statutory conflict of interest prohibitions; related to a June 2026 Zoning Board of Appeals meeting where Shega served as recording secretary on a hearing for a matter she participated in at the planning commission levelBreach of public trust and Open Meetings Act; related to accusations she did not submit meeting minutes in a timely mannerWillfully retaining and refusing to deliver public records; related to the previous charge and allegations Shega did not return “all Rock River Township documents and property” after receiving a demand letter from the clerk on 9/22/26
After reading the charges, Township Supervisor Gerry Melchiori pointed out that a previous supervisor had made an arrangement with the township attorney to have direct correspondence with members of the planning commission.
AHO: That’s still not our board policy. Just because somebody thinks they can do something — MELCHIORI: I’m just telling you that these people were given that permission —AHO: Those people were not authorized to have that permission
When Shega asked for a copy of the rule she violated, Township Clerk Heather Marsh provided a document titled "Rock River Township Legal Council Policy," reading,
"The Supervisor-Clerk-Treasurer-trustees-and Zoning Administrator May contact the legal council directly. Adopted by unanimous vote of the township board at the August 19, 2025 meeting."
During public comment, Shega said she felt blindsided by the strong demands for records and apologized if her participation as ZBA secretary was improper.
Further, Shega said, “I had no idea that there was an issue with me talking to an attorney. I had no idea any of this was coming, and I still find it hard to believe that it's come to this.”
After the meeting, Shega told My UP News the timing and focus of the charges seemed very coincidental. We asked her to explain what she meant:
“The coincidence, I suppose that Olivia and I were the only ones that voted to deny a permit for a convenience store on a couple of the board members’ properties. So that is coincidental. Another thing is, there's an election coming up in less than a month or a month, and I'm running for treasurer,” said Shega.
Kingery was not present at the meeting, and declined a request to comment from My UP News.
$11,000 elephant in the room
While discussing the charges against Kingery and Shega, Trustee Jim Rondeau made several references to what he describes as fake allegations; that his effort to develop land by the Eben Ice Caves has resulted in $11,000 of legal fees for the township.
“I got a call from a newspaper reporter quoting Tammy that I was in on blowing $11,000,” said Rondeau. “As it turns out, we know from the last meeting, Tammy and Cindy had a FOIA and they knew I wasn't calling my lawyer.”
A Sept. 9 article from the Mining Journal quotes former township trustee Rowan Bunce as saying the Rondeau brothers had been in “regular contact” with the township attorney — a claim Rondeau denies.
Township Clerk Marsh railed against criticism of Aho’s accusations of improper attorney contact, saying, “it was important enough for you to run to the news. But it's not important for us to take seriously as a board? Because it is against the law.”
At the meeting, Cindy Kallio pushed back on Rondeau, saying the FOIA only reflected attorney fees attributed to the lawsuit filed by Rondeau’s company — and did not specify costs related to communications with specific township officials.
“Prior to [the Wilderness Canyon LLC lawsuit], we didn’t even have a lawyer,” said Kallio.
Still, Rondeau maintained his frustration with his critics.
“I can't think of anything that would be closer to an actual classic case of defamation than that,” said Rondeau. “You knowingly spent the money at the lawyer and you went to the newspaper, and blamed me. It's amazing. It's absolutely disgusting.”
Looking ahead
The board voted 4-1 to call a hearing to review evidence behind Aho’s accusations and possibly vote on whether Shega and Kingery should be removed from their positions. The hearing is expected to occur on Oct. 27.
While the charges allege violations of not only township bylaws but also state law, it is unclear if the courts or sheriff’s office are involved.
Aho defended his accusations, saying the board has a duty to make sure everything is handled fairly, appropriately and legally.
“If we can't start running this right and start holding people accountable, and following the rules, it will just keep coming back to bite us because we're incapable of following rules and running anything properly,” said Aho.
My UP News spoke with one attendee, real estate attorney Mark Mueller, who said he recently moved to the area.
Mueller said he did not know enough about the ongoing situation to comment confidently, but after seeing what happened at the meeting, said, "I think that the board probably needs more involvement from lawyers than less."
Aho and Melchiori both declined interview requests from My UP News.
